content.introduction: The latest report from the Detroit Regional Chamber indicates that the Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rate slowed to 3.4% in July 2026, down from 3.5% in June 2026, marking the first decline in annual inflation rate since January 2026. Core inflation, excluding food and energy prices, also edged lower from 2.6% in June to 2.5% in July. This slowdown is largely attributed to the continued deceleration in housing price hikes, with the shelter index, which constitutes about one-third of the overall CPI basket, showing a steady rise. The overall outlook remains strong in Michigan, with solid consumer spending levels and a sustained low unemployment rate.

The latest report on inflation, as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), softened in April 2024, with a month-over-month increase of 0.3% and 3.4% increase over the prior year. The slowing is an encouraging sign as the 3% levels seen thus far in 2024 remain above target levels even though moderate by historical measures.

### Consumer Price Index Shows Inflation Softened in April 2024 [...] While consumer sentiment declined last month nationally, as consumers expressed concern about interest rates and inflation, the overall outlook remains strong in Michigan.
